description:
Finding: is_dev_mode() is defined independently on three separate AuthConfig structs (stoa_auth, reader, imap), each with different field sets and no cross-reference explaining why.

- stoa_auth::AuthConfig::is_dev_mode(): checks 6 fields (required, users, credential_file, client_certs, trusted_issuers, oidc_providers)
- reader::config::AuthConfig::is_dev_mode(): checks 5 fields (same minus operator_usernames check, which reader does not expose as a named field)  
- imap::config::AuthConfig::is_dev_mode(): checks only 3 fields (required, users, credential_file) — omits client_certs and trusted_issuers entirely

The imap AuthConfig struct legitimately does not have client_certs or trusted_issuers fields, so the divergence in field counts is structurally forced. However, none of the three implementations carries a comment explaining the relationship or confirming completeness against their own struct's full field list.

Maintenance hazard: if a new auth mechanism (e.g. oidc_providers) is added to imap::AuthConfig, is_dev_mode() will silently fail to account for it. The stoa_auth version serves as the canonical pattern but there is nothing binding imap or reader to stay in sync.

Suggested fix: add a comment to each is_dev_mode() implementation explicitly listing which fields it checks and confirming that all credential-granting fields are covered. Optionally add a compile-time struct exhaustiveness trick (destructure all fields in the body to get a compile error when a field is added).
title: is_dev_mode() duplicated with divergent field coverage across AuthConfig types
